text:
A: Hiya. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes, I can, thank you. Hello. I'm Imran, I'm in Huddersfield.
A: I'm Joanne. Sutton-in-Ashfield, near Mansfield. Sorry, I'm a bit nervous, I'm never sure where to look on these things.
B: No, that's fine. I'm the same, honestly. I keep looking at myself instead of the camera.
A: Oh, me too. What do you do, Imran?
B: Er, I do IT support. Part-time, for an accountancy firm and a dental practice. Fixing their laptops, printers, that sort of thing. And you?
A: I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. Serving dinners and that.
B: Oh, right. My partner's a teaching assistant at a primary. Saima. So I hear a lot about dinner time, actually. Mainly about the kids not eating their veg.
A: Oh, they don't! Anything green, it comes straight back. We do try. Does she like it, being a TA?
B: She does, yeah. She says it's tiring, but she likes the kids. She did a course for it, I think it was a Level 3, part of it online. Why, are you thinking about it?
A: Erm, I've sort of wondered. I don't know. I'd worry I'm not clever enough, you know, at my age. Sorry, that's a bit much for three minutes.
B: No, not at all. I did my qualifications in my thirties, evening study, online. Nobody minded my age. And from what Saima says, the good ones are the ones who are patient with the kids. You'd know which ones need what already, I imagine.
A: I do know all their allergies off by heart.
B: Well, there you go. That's half of it.
A: That's kind of you. What do you do when you're not working?
B: I walk a lot. Up Castle Hill, along the canal. I'm a bit obsessed with my step count, to be honest. And I read history, mostly.
A: Oh, I love history. What sort?
B: Partition, mostly. My parents are from Pakistan, so it's sort of family history as well, if that makes sense. And the Second World War.
A: It does. I read about mining round here. My dad was down the pit. There's so much the kids don't even know happened.
B: Yes. My dad worked nights in a textile mill when he came over. Same sort of thing. All those mills are flats now.
A: And the pits are retail parks. I walk the old railway lines, they used to take the coal out.
B: That's lovely, though, that they've kept those as paths.
A: It is. I sketch on there sometimes. Birds, mostly.
B: Is that your robin behind you?
A: It is, yeah. Is that, erm, is it Arabic, the one behind you? It's beautiful.
B: It is, yes. It's a verse from the Quran, Ayat al-Kursi. My mum gave it us. It's...
